Container.Name: eriphe
Container.Overview:
Eriphe is a self-hosted personal assistant: one assistant, always on at home, that you talk to from a web workspace, which remembers, works with the folders you open to it, and hands longer work to coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) signed in with your own account.
This container is Eriphe's launcher. It creates and keeps running Eriphe's own containers next to it: eriphe-core (the workspace, without any Docker access), eriphe-node (which runs each task in an isolated container) and a socket proxy that allows the node only the Docker calls it needs. The launcher listens on no port and runs nothing else; it applies the updates you start from the workspace, then updates itself. Their data is in the data folder below.
First start: the container's log gives the workspace's address and a setup code. Open the WebUI (https://the NAS:8443/setup), give the code to choose your password, and the wizard connects the AI account.
To remove it: docker exec eriphe eriphe-launcher uninstall (add --data to delete its data too), then remove the container.
Container.Requires: Docker 28 or later hides the NAS's own services from the tasks (Unraid 7.x has Docker 27: it works, with a warning in the log).

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: The launcher creates Eriphe's containers through it. eriphe-core and eriphe-node never get it: the node reaches Docker only through a socket proxy that allows its own calls.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Eriphe's data: eriphe-core's (core/: memory, accounts, keys), the node's (node/) and the launcher's (launcher/). Back it up; keep it out of the shares below.

Config.Name: Shares
Config.Description: The places whose folders you may give to Eriphe, as NAME=/PATH, comma-separated (NAME=/PATH:ro: never written to). Nothing is shared until you open a folder in the workspace (Settings, Folders): Eriphe reads it, and writes only in its results subfolder. Hidden folders, keys and appdata are always refused. Empty: no place.

Config.Name: Workspace port
Config.Description: The workspace's port on the NAS (HTTPS). If you change it, change the WebUI address of this template too.

Config.Name: API port
Config.Description: eriphe-core's port for the other devices you connect (Connect a device, in the workspace).

Config.Name: Listen address
Config.Description: The IPv4 address of the NAS the workspace and the API listen on. Empty: every IPv4 address. 127.0.0.1 when they are reached only through Tailscale or a reverse proxy on the NAS.

Config.Name: Version
Config.Description: Empty: the releases (the image's tag). A release (0.8.0, or 0.8 for its fixes) stays on it; edge follows the main branch, for testers.

Config.Name: Node name
Config.Description: This NAS's name among your devices (lowercase letters, digits, dashes). Empty: the server's name.

Config.Name: Node labels
Config.Description: What agents can require of this machine, comma-separated (gpu).

Config.Name: Model server
Config.Description: A model server this NAS lends to Eriphe through its tunnel, without opening a port: http://eriphe-ollama:11434 for an Ollama container on the eriphe-system network (no port published). Empty: none.

Config.Name: Mode
Config.Description: core: Eriphe runs here, with this NAS as its first device. node: this NAS joins an Eriphe that runs elsewhere (then give the three settings below, from Connect a device in its workspace).

Config.Name: eriphe-core to join (node mode)
Config.Description: Its address, as Connect a device gives it: https://192.0.2.10:8800.

Config.Name: Join token (node mode)
Config.Description: Single use, for this name, valid 24 h: only for the first start.

Config.Name: CA hash (node mode)
Config.Description: sha256:... of eriphe-core's certificate authority, which the node checks.
